SUBJECT:       CHRISTOPHER M. CRANE CLEAN ENERGY CENTER – REQUEST FOR
               INFORMATION FOR POST-APPROVAL SITE INSPECTION FOR LICENSE
               RENEWAL, PHASE III, INSPECTION REPORT 05000289/2027011

Dear Christopher Mudrick:

On February 22, 2027, the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) will begin a license
renewal (LR) post-approval inspection at your Christopher M. Crane Clean Energy Center
(CCEC). The inspection will be conducted in accordance with Inspection Procedure (IP) 71003,
“Post-Approval Site Inspection for License Renewal,” dated August 11, 2023 (Agencywide
Documents Access and Management System (ADAMS) Accession No. ML22245A071). CCEC,
formerly known as Three Mile Island Nuclear Station, Unit 1, entered the period of extended
operation (PEO) in April 2014. Constellation Energy Generation, formerly Exelon Generation,
announced the intent for its permanent shutdown in May 2017, confirmed its permanent
shutdown in May 2019, and permanently shut down in September 2019.

Under the guidance of Inspection Manual Chapter 2562, “Light-Water Reactor Inspection
Program for Restart of Reactor Facilities following Permanent Cessation of Power Operations,”
dated April 24, 2025, this inspection will be conducted to ensure key LR activities, such as aging
management programs (AMPs), have been reestablished prior to restart at CCEC as part of the
Crane Restart Inspection Plan (ML25114A121). IP 71003 also describes how this inspection
reviews the implementation of license conditions, regulatory commitments, time-limited aging
analyses, and AMPs against the implementation schedules that extend into the PEO. While the
previous IP 71003 LR inspections at Three Mile Island Nuclear Station, Unit 1 did not identify
any inspection findings, substantial time has elapsed since its permanent shutdown in 2019.
Furthermore, substantial portions of the LR-related AMP activities were discontinued in
preparation for the permanent shutdown. Therefore, as part of your restart activities, this
inspection will focus on assessing the adequacy of the completed and/or planned activities and
programs described in the regulatory commitments and licensee conditions, which had been
incorporated into your renewed license at the time of the 20-year license extension.

To minimize the inspection impact on the site and to ensure a productive inspection for both
parties, we have enclosed a request for information needed for the inspection. It is important
 C. Mudrick                                        2


that all these documents are up-to-date and complete to minimize the number of additional
documents requested during the preparation and/or the on-site portions of the inspection.
Insofar as possible, the information should be provided electronically to the lead inspector. This
information request has been divided into two groups:

•   The first group lists information necessary for our initial inspection scoping and in-office
    preparation activities. During the in-office preparation activities, the inspector(s) will identify
    as much as possible the information and activities to be reviewed during the inspection. This
    information should be provided to the inspector(s) by January 25, 2027.
•   The second group includes the additional information required for the inspector(s) to review
    the selected activities. This information should be available to the inspector(s) 1 week before
    arriving onsite, by February 12, 2027.
•   It is also requested that corrective action documents and/or questions developed during the
    inspection be provided to the inspector(s) as the documents are generated.

The lead inspector for this LR inspection is Joon S. Park, a Senior Reactor Inspector from the
NRC’s CNRI Region III office. If there are any questions about the inspection or the information
requested in the enclosure, please contact the lead inspector at 630-829-9715 or via email at
Joon.Park@nrc.gov.

This letter does not contain new or amended information collection requirements subject to the
Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (44 U.S.C. 3501 et seq.). Existing information collection
requirements were approved by the Office of Management and Budget, Control Number 3150-
0011. The NRC may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, a
request for information or an information collection requirement unless the requesting document
displays a currently valid Office of Management and Budget Control Number.

This letter and its enclosure will be made available for public inspection and copying at
http://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/adams.html and at the NRC Public Document Room in
accordance with Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations 2.390, “Public Inspections,
Exemptions, Requests for Withholding.”

      DOCUMENT REQUEST FOR POST-APPROVAL SITE INSPECTION FOR LICENSE
                               RENEWAL


Inspection Report:           05000289/2027011


Inspection Dates:            February 22, 2027 – March 12, 2027


Inspection Procedures:       IP 71003, “Post-Approval Site Inspection for License Renewal”
                             Phase III


Lead Inspector:              Joon S. Park
                             630-829-9715
                             Joon.Park@nrc.gov


I.    Information Requested Prior to the Inspection Preparation Week

      This section of the request identifies general information that will help the inspectors
      understand the applicable administrative procedures and overall status of license
      renewal activities. The information requested herein is not aimed at a particular
      regulatory commitment, license condition, time-limited aging analysis (TLAA), or aging
      management program (AMP).

      The following information is requested by January 25, 2027, or sooner, to facilitate
      inspection preparation. If you have any questions regarding this information, please
      contact the lead inspector. Please provide the information electronically in “PDF” files,
      Excel, or other searchable formats, preferably on a station/corporate online portal for
      document sharing. The files should contain descriptive names, be indexed, and
      hyperlinked to facilitate ease of use. Information in “lists” should contain enough
      information to be easily understood by someone who has knowledge of light-water
      reactor technology.

      1. Provide copies of the following site-specific documents:

          •   Corrective Action Program governing procedures
          •   Operating Experience Program procedure
          •   License Renewal Implementation Program procedures that govern the following
              processes:
              o Regulatory commitment change
              o License renewal requirements management
              o 10 CFR 54.37(b) reviews
              o Turnover and preparation for PEO “re-entry”
              o Self-assessments / effectiveness reviews for the AMPs
          •   Technical Requirements Manual
          •   Quality Assurance Topical Report (QATR), or equivalent

      2. Provide a list of your license renewal commitments with a description of the overall
         completion status of action items associated with each commitment, including AMPs
         and TLAAs.



                                                                                       Enclosure

       3. Specify the latest revision of the Updated Final Safety Analysis Report (UFSAR) at
          the time of the permanent shutdown in 2019, and provide copies of all approved
          pending UFSAR change notices that had not been incorporated into the UFSAR prior
          to the permanent shutdown.

       4. Provide a list of your AMPs, copies of associated program basis documents, a list of
          the action tracking items and preventative maintenance IDs (PMIDs) credited for
          each AMP and TLAA.

       5. For AMPs that are related to one-time inspection programs, provide a list of
          completed one-time inspections that contain the work order numbers, description of
          the inspections completed, inspected component identification, date of the
          completion, and the associated AMPs.

       6. Provide documentation of any correspondence between the licensee and the NRC,
          after the license was issued, associated with regulatory issues affecting the license
          renewal commitment. For example, this may include notifications of commitment
          changes, or license amendment requests, affecting license conditions or license
          renewal commitments.

        7. Provide the station’s Environmental Qualification (EQ) binder for all components
           within the scope of EQ that have been qualified for sixty or more years, including
           information on component ID, component description, system, environment
           category, and qualified life, along with the station’s EQ program procedures.

       8. Provide current management and license renewal organizational charts.

       9. Provide electronic copies of any internal/external self-assessments and associated
          corrective action documents generated in preparation for the inspection.


II.    Information Requested to Be Available One Week Prior to Inspectors’ Arrival On-
       Site (February 12, 2027)

       1. Documentation demonstrating completion of license renewal commitments
          completed as of the inspection date. For example, this may be in the form of a binder
          for each commitment which includes the implementing documentation and
          references.


III.   Information Requested to Be Provided Throughout the Inspection

       1. Copies of any corrective action documents generated from inspector questions or
          queries during this inspection.

       2. Copies of the list of questions submitted by the team members and the
          status/resolution of the information requested (provide daily during the inspection to
          each team member).

If you have any questions regarding the information requested, please contact the lead
inspector.
